the structure of the polysaccharide capsular material of the yeast Cryptococcus neo formans and its role in the pathogenesis of cryptococcosis.
the structural biology of Cryptococcus capsular polysaccharide, which is the primary virulence factor for this pathogenic fungus.
the antigenic and biological properties of mutant strains of C. neoformans with defects in the biosynthesis of capsular glucuronoxylomanan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
O acetylated and non-O-acetylated GXM are antigenically and biologically distinct.
the O acetylation is a critical structural determinant of GXM, while xylosylation plays a more subtle role.
O acetylated GXM is a major target antigen in cryptococcal infections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
O acetylated GXM is more important in immune recognition than is xylosyl-GXM.
loss of O-acetyl groups in GXM is a more important determinant of the antigenic properties of C. neoformans and of the pathogenesis of cryptococcosis than is the loss of xylosyl side chains.
loss of O-acetylation has a more significant impact on the immunological properties of the GXM molecule than loss of xylosyl groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O acetylated GXM is a better target for anti-GXM MAAbs than is xylosylated GXM.
loss of O acetate and xylose from GXM does not alter the ability of the organism to resist phagocytosisis, but it does impact other aspects of cryptococcal virulence.
O acetylations and xylosylation are not required for virulence in a mouse model of cryptococcosis.
